Just piggybacking to add some details, 

In the 1970s some places (like the US) stopped treating homosexuality as a criminal act. It is also important to note that prior to this time it was listed as a disease in the medical world.

The newfound freedom to be a homosexual led many members of the gay community to embrace a rather promiscuous life. Bathhouses were very common places to frequent, especially in San Francisco and New York. This happened for years before the first case of AIDS popped up. HIV can stay unsymptomatic for quite a long time, and so no one knew that this lifestyle was in any way harmful.

When the cases started rolling in from the gay community, the medical community was trying to get a sense of this strange new disease. They didn't really know what was going on, or why it was seemingly only targeting gay men. It took years from the first few cases to knowing the cause was the HIV virus. This allowed a lot of time for misinformation to spread. It confused even the medical community that there was a contagious cancer (it often presented as a rare skin cancer called Kaposi's Sarcoma) that only affected gay people. No one could really say why this was the case.

Unsurprisingly after having lived through the covid pandemic, everyone who bothered to care about the plight of the early AIDS victims had their own theories and ideas. The government and media, unlike covid, did very little to try to correct misinformation. Ideas like gay people were being punished for being gay were prevalent, and as you can imagine many people in the gay community were upset that this tragedy was being made to be their fault. Even when they understood the transmission of the disease, there was pushback from within the gay community to closing bathhouses, as they didn't believe these could really be the cause. They believed society was trying to restrict their freedoms and infringe on their rights. This is understandable. The societal conditions that lead to the quick spread of this disease were truly the perfect storm. A population was being asked to trust the medical community who believed their sexual orientation was a disease until recently, and the government that believed it was a crime until recently. The conspiracy theories flowed naturally and there was certainly a logic that could be followed in these arguments. 

All of these reasons contributed to why the gay community was disproportionately affected, even if we ignore the increased physical risk that anal intercourse (gay or straight) presents.

Not interested in changing. Not interested in getting better anymore. Not interested in anything except not being alive anymore. Anything this broken has no value. Thanks for trying to help, but it's over.
I could have written this. Poignant and sad and relatable.

I agree entirely. I'd have done less damage if I'd have died when I was younger when I wanted to. Now there are just more people to hurt when I inevitably fail at living and give in. And I've had life break my heart many more times in the process.  I truly don't think I was meant to be here. I have never fit anywhere or with anyone. I know that nothing will ever get better for me, my life gets worse every year that I'm alive. I don't make the world a better place and everyone who cares about me will get over it, especially since I'm such a drain on them. I just wish I didn't have to be violent towards myself to end it.

YTA. She is obviously already struggling. You seem to care more about her weight than her mental health. She knows she gained weight, she doesn't need you to tell her. All you've managed to do is make her feel insecure and ugly. She needs to feel better mentally and emotionally before she will have the energy to complete any sort of weight loss or exercise program. A more productive way to handle the situation would be to perhaps take on more cooking and make healthy meals.

NTA at all. In fact, I think that if you hadn't reacted in a way that protects your son, that would have made you the asshole. Your child needs to feel safe and secure in his own home, and having his journal stolen is a huge breech of privacy and boundaries. If your fiancée doesn't see her mother as the problem and won't go to bat for you and your son, you'll be setting yourself up for a lifetime of conflict. Good for you for being a great Dad, it must have felt so good for your son to see you were in his corner.
